To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the ultrafiltration technique in conjunction with PIXE measurement can be used to determine elemental concentrations in subfraction of human blood plasma, and (2) the concentrations of Cu and Zn in the ultrafiltrate of EDTA-plasma were higher in breast cancer patients than in healthy subjects.
the concentrations of Cu in the ultrafiltrate of plasma from healthy persons were significantly higher than those of the cancer patients.
the ultrafiltration technique in conjunction with PIXE is a suitable method for investigation of the distribution of Cu, Zn and other trace elements in blood plasma subfractions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for investigation of trace elements in subfractions obtained by ultrafiltration from plasma.
the investigation of blood plasma ultrafiltration as a new approach to the study of metal binding proteins and the determination of their concentrations in blood.
the determination of the elemental composition of plasma subfractions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Cu, Zn and possibly Fe are present in blood plasma as complexes with low molecular weight substances.
the ultrafiltration in the presence of EDTA followed by PIXE measurement is an effective technique for the determination of loosely-bound Cu in blood plasma.
the Cu concentration in blood plasma subfractions is not a reliable parameter for monitoring of the Cu status of the human body.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

ultrafiltration in the presence of EDTA is a suitable method for the investigation of loosely bound Cu, Zn and possibly Fe in the blood plasma subfraction containing substances with molecular weight under 10, 000.
the Cu content of the ultrafiltrate is not significantly different between healthy and diseased subjects.
the Cu content of blood plasma ultrafiltrates is higher in cancer patients than in healthy persons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the concentration of loosely bound Cu in the ultrafiltration fraction is significantly higher in the blood plasma of breast cancer patients than in healthy subjects.
the Cu content in blood plasma is not a good marker for Cu status in the body.
the Cu concentration in the blood plasma subfractions is significantly higher than in the total plasma.
